claims.text: Lower-temperature synthesis of PtPdCoCuNi nanoparticles on SiO2 promotes rapid precursor trapping.
Rapid precursor trapping minimizes atomic diffusion.
Minimizing atomic diffusion yields a homogeneous, single-phase PtPdCoCuNi alloy.
Lower-temperature synthesis produces isolated Pt/Pd active sites.
A homogeneous solution of near-equiatomic PtPdCoCuNi precursors on SiO2 is the proposed initial state.
Room-temperature or slightly elevated-temperature one-step colloidal synthesis can kinetically trap the precursors.
Synthesis at 80–120 °C increases atomic mobility relative to synthesis near room temperature.
Reduced precursor mobility at lower temperature traps individual atoms as they incorporate into the forming alloy.
Kinetic trapping at lower temperature minimizes diffusion-driven phase separation.
A uniform, single-phase HEA structure containing isolated active sites is favorable for catalytic charge transfer.
Higher synthesis temperatures permit greater atomic mobility and can lead to phase segregation.
Higher-temperature synthesis produces fewer isolated active centers than lower-temperature synthesis.
Lower-temperature nanoparticles will have greater atomic homogeneity than nanoparticles synthesized at 80–120 °C.
Lower-temperature nanoparticles will contain a higher proportion of isolated Pt/Pd sites than the high-temperature baseline.
Lower-temperature nanoparticles will show improved nitrobenzene hydrogenation performance, potentially including increased aniline yield.
The proposed comparison holds precursor concentrations, solvent, support, and reaction time constant while varying synthesis temperature.
The hypothesis is intended primarily for near-equiatomic PtPdCoCuNi nanoparticles on SiO2 made by one-step colloidal synthesis under controlled solvent conditions.
